title: Local bounded models with finite constant graded terms
statement: Let C be a small site with final object X [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], B a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and K in its derived category of B-module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let integers a<b satisfy H^q(K)=0 outside [a,b] [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and assume that every H^q(K) is locally a constant sheaf of a finitely generated B-module [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There is a covering {U_i -> X} and, on each slice C/U_i [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], a cochain complex P_i, a family of finite B-modules M_i^q vanishing outside [a,b], isomorphisms P_i^q = constant(M_i^q) for all q, and a derived isomorphism K|U_i = Q(P_i). The differentials of P_i are arbitrary sheaf morphisms; they are not required to be induced by module maps.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, proof of the strengthened bounded constant-model assertion

proof.text: Apply the local finite constant extension tower theorem to K and [a,b]. Its output is a covering and, on each slice, a tower of width (b-a).toNat. It records only distinguished triangles with finite constant single attachments, not a complex.

source.place: Tag 094G, proof of lemma-locally-constant, triangles in the induction before chain realization

proof.text: Prove by induction on the finite tower a generic realization statement for any additive functor S from B-modules to any abelian category A. The zero-width tower is already a single object in degree a. Choose the coefficient module at a and zero modules at every other degree; the single complex has the corresponding terms, because S preserves zero objects.

source.place: Tag 094G, proof of lemma-locally-constant, triangles in the induction before chain realization

proof.text: For a successor tower K to L to single(S(M),a+n), realize L by induction as Q(E), with E zero above a+n. Conjugate the boundary by the isomorphism L=Q(E), and use the bounded-top chain-representative theorem to obtain an actual chain map f:E to single(S(M),a+n). Its mapping cocone has degree q term E^q direct sum single(S(M),a+n)^(q-1). If q=a+n+1, E^q is zero and the other term is S(M); otherwise the single term is zero and the result is E^q. Choose M at the new top degree and the old coefficient modules elsewhere. These give finite terms and the exact interval bounds.

source.place: Tag 094G, proof of lemma-locally-constant, triangles in the induction before chain realization

proof.text: The localized mapping-cocone triangle is distinguished. Rotate it and the tower triangle. The inductive isomorphism L=Q(E), the identity of the single object, and Q(f)=eL.inv composed with the boundary identify the first arrows. The morphism-of-triangles axiom gives a triangle isomorphism; its third component identifies K[1] with Q(mappingCocone(f))[1]. Shift back by -1 and cancel the shifts to obtain the required isomorphism K=Q(P). Apply this realization on each covering slice, and use a+(b-a).toNat=b to obtain the original bounds.

Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/AlternatingConst and Factorizations/CM5a concern different meanings of constant; no constant graded local model theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_site_bounded_constant_graded_model
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition]
    [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks]
    (X : C) (hX : IsTerminal X)
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B))]
    [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (Sheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over U) (ModuleCat.{u} B))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B)))
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a < b)
    (hvan : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B)) q).obj K))
    (hloc : ∀ (q : ℤ) (V : C),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ V),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J V ∧
        ∀ i : I, ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} B, Module.Finite B M ∧ Nonempty
          ((J.toGrothendieck.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} B) (U i)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B)) q).obj K) ≅
            (constantSheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)).obj M)) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X),
      Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J X ∧
      ∀ i : I, ∃ P : CochainComplex
          (Sheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)) ℤ,
        ∃ M : ℤ → ModuleCat.{u} B,
          (∀ q : ℤ, Module.Finite B (M q)) ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (M q)) ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty (P.X q ≅
            (constantSheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)).obj (M q))) ∧
          Nonempty
            ((@Functor.mapDerivedCategory _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
                (J.toGrothendieck.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} B) (U i))
                (Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products _) _
                ⟨fun _ _ _ ↦ PreservesColimitsOfSize.preservesColimitsOfShape
                  (self := Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits
                    (Functor.sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous
                      (Over.forget (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)
                      (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) J.toGrothendieck))⟩).obj K ≅
              DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)

split_report.summary: The cohomological induction part of Tag 094G is separated from the finite simultaneous differential-descent argument, which is proved in Lean. The only remaining hole is this graded construction. The derived boundary chain representative is proved separately using the canonical t-structure, removing the two fraction nodes from this route. Finite-free local lifting across an epimorphism is also proved, so the cycles-to-homology epimorphism can be used directly without the presheaf-quotient detour.
